selection.rule: the newest batch, by anchor_ts, that has an `anchors` row (i.e. is a scheduled rebalance) and submitted at least one order; rehearsal (R*) batches are excluded from automatic selection and can only be scored by being named

E1_topup_residual.note: UNDETERMINED if no maker leg filled — nothing to have sized a residual from

readback_used.rule: the first reconciliation at or after the scored anchor

E4_row_self_consistency.twin_limit: 0 rows with filled_notional set and submit_ts None (tonight 77)
E4_row_self_consistency.limit: 0 rows with avg_fill_px set and filled_notional == 0 (tonight 47)
E4_row_self_consistency.q3_limit: 0 rows with terminal_reason=='filled' and filled_notional None (day-wide: 1)
E4_row_self_consistency.q4_limit: 0 rows with last_fill_ts < submit_ts. THE EXAM'S SUBJECT CANNOT CONTAIN THIS: all 204 measured instances are `protective_flatten` rows and the selector excludes ladder batches, so a 0 here is structural, not evidence. Read `day_wide` for the population that has it.
E4_row_self_consistency.day_wide_caliber: every order row in the day, ALL batches including the ladder's — reported without a verdict, because the exam's verdict is defined over its selected subject and must not silently change population

E5_position_equals_intent.denominator: target_w x this anchor's own anchors.target_gross (a STOCK: what we meant to HOLD). NOT intended_notional, which is the anchor's DELTA and only equals the target when the book starts flat.
E5_position_equals_intent.population: judged on names that TRADED; a name the venue refused has ratio 0 and is E3's subject — pooling makes E5 fail whenever E3 does and stops it being an independent question. Pooled figure reported, not judged on.
E5_position_equals_intent.caliber: computed from position_readback and the orders' intended_notional — INDEPENDENT of §4-5b's implementation, which changed on 2026-07-26
E5_position_equals_intent.limit: median in [0.9, 1.1] (the doubling reads ~2.0 — and so did every REBALANCING anchor under the old flow denominator, which is why that reading alone is not evidence of a doubling)

E5b_5b_silent.role: CORROBORATION for E5, not the criterion itself

E6_cost_comparable.measurement_complete_source: cost_buckets.bucket_fills over the rebalance legs: every fill known, priced, and fee-known (finite; all-USDT or converted). NOT pilot_metrics.m1's bit — see `m1_measurement_complete`.
E6_cost_comparable.cost_bps_displayed_source: cost_buckets over the rebalance legs — the SAME rows and the SAME rule that produced `measurement_complete`, hence the same population the verdict rests on. `abs_bps_measured` is m1's `c_bps_overall` caliber (fee + |slip|); `bps_measured` is `c_bps_net_overall`'s (fee + SIGNED slip). Rounded to 4 decimals — m1's own precision — so the two figures on this page are comparable digit by digit; the unrounded values are in `buckets`. None = nothing was measured, which is not 0.

carrier_consistency.rule: round 3, 2026-09-13 (researcher REVIEW §3.C): E6 may PASS only when the bucket population and m1's population are the SAME SET — asserted on the counts and the notional mass each carrier reports for itself, pooled AND per regime, not on a flag — and the two bps figures agree within the stated tolerance in BOTH calibers. Otherwise this criterion is NOT a PASS and the disagreement is named in `why_not`. m1 is frozen (ops/check_metrics_freeze); nothing here edits or re-implements it.

E6_cost_comparable.c_bps_overall_source: pilot_metrics.m1 (FROZEN), over M1'S OWN population — it drops rows whose `side`, anchor mid or fill price it cannot read and keeps fee-unknown rows in its denominator at fee 0. Comparable with `cost_bps_displayed` only when `carrier_consistency.consistent` is True.
E6_cost_comparable.caliber: per-DAY aggregate: (sum fee + sum |slippage|) / sum filled_notional, in bps, over every filled order of the day; NOT a per-fill figure

protective_flatten_cost.caliber: event-driven exit cost, EXCLUDED from c (which measures rebalance execution quality, the quantity §4-1's limit was set for). Reported, not discarded. `fee_paid` is the sum over the rows whose fee we ACTUALLY read — never a zero standing in for rows we did not.

protective_flatten_buckets.measured_over: MEASURED fills only — a fill with a usable price (finite positive avg_fill_px AND mid_at_anchor) AND a known fee (fee_paid not None and finite; a raw mixed-asset fee with fee_all_usdt=False and no fee_conversion is NOT known). An unpriced or fee-unknown fill is excluded from numerator AND denominator; it is not a zero-cost fill. bps is None when nothing was measured.

E6_cost_comparable.rule: if measurement_complete is not True, c is a LOWER BOUND and MUST NOT be compared against the 9.0bps limit — the rule is unchanged from the pre-registration; only the prediction was amended (and, W2-R1, the completeness bit is now derived from the three buckets, since m1 is frozen). Round 3: a complete measurement is NECESSARY and no longer SUFFICIENT — the verdict also requires `carrier_consistency.consistent`, because a bit derived from one population cannot certify a number computed over another

buckets.measured_over: MEASURED fills only — a fill with a usable price (finite positive avg_fill_px AND mid_at_anchor) AND a known fee (fee_paid not None and finite; a raw mixed-asset fee with fee_all_usdt=False and no fee_conversion is NOT known). An unpriced or fee-unknown fill is excluded from numerator AND denominator; it is not a zero-cost fill. bps is None when nothing was measured.

E6_cost_comparable.bucket_rule: W2 2026-09-12: the rebalance legs (maker + topup_taker) under the three-bucket rule of anchor_loop.neutrality_price. `bps_measured` is over MEASURED fills only and is None when none was measured; it equals m1's `c_bps_net_overall` exactly when every fill is measured, and diverges when m1 keeps fee-unknown notional in its denominator at fee 0. The verdict keys on `measurement_complete` (bucket-derived); `c_bps_overall` stays m1's figure and may be non-finite — see `c_bps_overall_is_finite`.
